title: The accounting equation and why every entry has two sides
content: Assets = Liabilities + Equity. Every financial event is recorded so that the equation still holds afterwards, which is why a journal entry always has at least one debit and at least one credit and why their totals are equal. This is not a convention that can be relaxed for convenience: a single-sided entry does not describe an event, it describes half of one, and the missing half is always a real account somewhere. When you cannot name the second side of an entry you do not yet understand the transaction, and the correct action is to hold it unposted rather than to force it into a suspense account and move on. Expanded for a trading period: Assets = Liabilities + Opening Equity + Revenue - Expenses - Distributions, which is the reason revenue and expense accounts close into retained earnings at period end.

structured_data.expanded: Assets = Liabilities + Opening Equity + Revenue - Expenses - Distributions

title: What a debit and a credit actually do to each type of account
content: Debit and credit are directions, not good and bad. A debit increases assets and expenses and decreases liabilities, equity and revenue. A credit does the reverse: it increases liabilities, equity and revenue and decreases assets and expenses. The common error is to read 'credit' as money arriving because that is what a bank statement says; a bank statement is written from the bank's point of view, where your deposit is the bank's liability. From the company's own books, cash arriving is a DEBIT to Cash and Bank. Contra accounts invert the expectation of their family: Accumulated Depreciation is an asset-family account with a normal CREDIT balance because it exists to reduce the cost account it sits against.

structured_data.trap: a bank statement is written from the bank's perspective and inverts the sign a business's own books use

title: Normal balance, and reading it off the live chart of accounts instead of assuming it
content: Every account has a normal balance, D or C, and it is recorded on the account row itself in public.gl_accounts.normal_balance rather than inferred from the account's type. Infer it and you will be wrong on exactly the accounts that matter: Accumulated Depreciation is type asset with normal balance C, and a revenue-family account used to record a reversal can sit in debit legitimately for a period. The rule for the accountant seat is to read normal_balance from the row before judging whether a balance is unusual, and to treat a balance sitting on the wrong side as a question to investigate rather than as an error to correct by posting the difference away.

structured_data.example_of_the_trap: 1650 Accumulated Depreciation is type=asset with normal_balance=C

title: What a journal entry must carry before it may be posted
content: A postable journal entry carries a date that places it in the correct accounting period, a description that a reader who was not present can understand, at least two lines whose debits equal their credits to the smallest unit of currency, an account code on every line that exists and is active in the chart of accounts, and a reference back to the source document that caused it. An entry missing the source reference is not a bookkeeping shortcut, it is an unauditable figure: three months later nobody can say whether it happened. If any of these is missing the entry is held, not posted, and the missing item is what the accountant chases.

title: How posting to the general ledger works and why the ledger is not the journal
content: The journal is the chronological record of what happened; the ledger is the same events reorganised by account. Posting is the act of moving each journal line onto its account. The two must always agree, because the ledger contains no information the journal did not already carry: if a ledger balance cannot be rebuilt by replaying the journal lines for that account, something has been written to the ledger that was never journalised, and that is a control failure rather than a reconciliation difference. In this estate the journal is public.gl_journal with its lines in public.gl_journal_lines, and the account-level views are derived; the derivation direction is one-way and must stay that way.

structured_data.invariant: every ledger balance is reproducible by replaying journal lines

title: What a trial balance proves, and the four errors it cannot see
content: A trial balance lists every account balance and shows that total debits equal total credits. That is all it proves. It cannot see an entry omitted entirely, an entry posted twice in full, an entry posted to the wrong account of the right type, or two errors that happen to offset. So a balanced trial balance is a necessary condition for correct books and nowhere near a sufficient one, and reporting 'the trial balance balances' as evidence that the accounts are right is a claim the instrument does not support. The checks that catch what it cannot are reconciliation to external sources, review of account movement against expectation, and cut-off testing at the period boundary.

cannot_detect: duplicate posting of a whole entry
posting to the wrong account of the right type

title: Accrual basis and cash basis, and which question each one answers
content: On the cash basis a transaction is recorded when money moves. On the accrual basis it is recorded when the economic event happens: revenue when the performance obligation is satisfied, expense when the resource is consumed, regardless of when cash follows. The two answer different questions. Cash tells you whether you can pay next week; accrual tells you whether the period's trading was profitable. A business running on accrual still needs a cash view, which is why a cash flow statement exists separately from the income statement. Mixing the bases within one set of books, for example recognising revenue on accrual and costs on cash, produces a margin that is not a margin at all, and it is the single most common way a small company's profit figure becomes fiction.

structured_data.accrual_basis: record when the economic event occurs
structured_data.failure_mode: mixing the two within one set of books distorts margin

title: The accrual entry: an expense incurred that has not been invoiced
content: When a period ends and a cost has been incurred but no supplier invoice has arrived, the cost still belongs to that period. Debit the expense account and credit an accrual liability. When the invoice arrives, the accrual is reversed and the invoice posted normally, so the expense is not counted twice. Where the cost relates to goods or services already received, the estate holds account 2250 GRNI (Goods Received Not Invoiced) for exactly this, distinct from 2200 Accrued Expenses which carries the broader case. The discipline that matters is that the accrual is reversed on a defined date rather than left standing: an accrual nobody clears becomes a permanent liability for a cost that was invoiced and paid months ago.

structured_data.entry: Dr expense / Cr 2200 Accrued Expenses (or 2250 GRNI where goods were received)
structured_data.on_invoice: reverse the accrual, then post the invoice normally
structured_data.risk: an unreversed accrual double-counts the liability

title: The prepayment: cash paid now for a period that has not happened yet
content: An annual software subscription paid in one instalment is not one month's expense. On payment, debit 1400 Prepaid Expenses and credit cash; then in each period of the term, release the portion consumed by debiting the expense account and crediting 1400. The balance left in 1400 at any moment should equal the unconsumed remainder of every open prepayment, and that is a testable statement: list the open contracts, compute the remainder, compare. If they do not agree, a release has been missed or a contract has been cancelled without unwinding. For a company whose costs are dominated by annual tool subscriptions, the prepayment schedule is the difference between a monthly cost line that means something and one that spikes with the renewal calendar.

structured_data.on_payment: Dr 1400 Prepaid Expenses / Cr 1000 Cash & Bank
structured_data.test: 1400 balance equals the sum of unconsumed remainders across open contracts

title: Deferred revenue: money received before the obligation is satisfied
content: Cash received is not revenue earned. When a customer or supplier pays before the company has done what the payment is for, debit cash and credit 2400 Deferred Revenue, a liability, because at that moment the company owes a service rather than owns a profit. Revenue is recognised, by moving the balance from 2400 to the relevant revenue account, only when the obligation is satisfied. This is the entry that most often gets skipped in a young marketplace, and skipping it overstates revenue in the month money arrives and understates it in the month work is done, which makes every trend line drawn through those months wrong.

structured_data.principle: cash received is a liability until the obligation is satisfied

title: The receivable lifecycle, from recognition to cash or write-off
content: A receivable is created when revenue is recognised but not yet collected: debit 1100 Accounts Receivable (or 1110 Supplier Commission Receivable for amounts owed by suppliers) and credit the revenue account. It is cleared when cash arrives: debit cash, credit the receivable. Nothing else may clear it silently. Ageing the balance by invoice date is what turns a receivable total into information: a single figure of amounts owed says nothing about whether it will be collected, whereas the same figure split by how long each amount has been outstanding says almost everything. Amounts that will not be collected leave through the bad-debt route, which is a decision that is recorded, not an adjustment that is quietly made.

structured_data.information: age the balance by invoice date; a single total is not a collectability assessment

title: The payable lifecycle, and why a bill is recorded before it is paid
content: When a supplier invoice is received, debit the expense or asset account and credit 2000 Accounts Payable. When it is paid, debit 2000 and credit cash. Recording the bill at receipt rather than at payment is what makes the period's cost complete and what makes the payables balance a real statement of what the company owes today. A company that posts only at payment cannot answer 'what do we owe' at all, because the answer lives in an inbox rather than in the ledger. The payables balance should be reconcilable to a list of unpaid invoices at any moment; when it is not, either a bill has been paid without clearing the payable or a payment has cleared a payable that was never recorded.

structured_data.on_payment: Dr 2000 Accounts Payable / Cr 1000 Cash & Bank
structured_data.test: the 2000 balance equals the list of unpaid supplier invoices

title: Depreciation, the contra account, and what the choice of method actually decides
content: A fixed asset is capitalised at cost in 1600 Fixed Assets - Cost and its consumption is spread across the periods that benefit from it. The periodic entry debits 6400 Depreciation Expense and credits 1650 Accumulated Depreciation, a contra-asset account, so the original cost stays visible and the wear is visible beside it; net book value is the difference. Straight line spreads the depreciable amount evenly over the useful life; reducing balance takes a constant percentage of the falling carrying amount and therefore charges more early. Neither is more correct in the abstract: the method should follow the pattern in which the asset's benefit is actually consumed, and the useful life and any residual value are estimates that are reviewed rather than set once. Which method and life a specific entity must use, and any tax treatment that differs from the accounting treatment, is resolved from the applicable accounting framework and the current tax authority, not from this record.

structured_data.capitalise: Dr 1600 Fixed Assets - Cost / Cr cash or payable
structured_data.periodic: Dr 6400 Depreciation Expense / Cr 1650 Accumulated Depreciation

title: Disposing of an asset: the gain or loss is a residual, never a plug
content: On disposal, remove both sides of the asset: credit 1600 Fixed Assets - Cost for the original cost and debit 1650 Accumulated Depreciation for the depreciation charged to date. Debit whatever consideration was received. The difference is the gain or loss, credited to 4300 Gain on Asset Disposal or debited to 6500 Loss on Asset Disposal. The figure falls out of the entry; it is never chosen first and the entry made to fit it. A disposal that appears to produce an implausible gain almost always means depreciation was under-charged over the asset's life, and that is the finding, not the gain.

structured_data.entry: Dr 1650 accumulated depreciation + Dr cash received / Cr 1600 cost, with the residual to 4300 or 6500
structured_data.diagnostic: an implausible gain usually means depreciation was under-charged

title: Bad debt: recognising that a receivable will not be collected
content: When a receivable is judged uncollectable, the expense belongs to the books, not the silence. Debit 6900 Refunds & Bad Debt and credit the receivable, and record why the judgement was made and on what date. Two things follow. First, the judgement is evidenced: an amount unpaid past its terms is not automatically bad, and an amount whose counterparty has vanished is bad regardless of how recent it is. Second, if the amount is later recovered, the recovery is posted as its own event rather than by deleting the write-off, because deleting it would erase the fact that the company once judged it lost. A pattern of write-offs against a single counterparty class is a commercial finding to report, not just an accounting entry to make.

structured_data.entry: Dr 6900 Refunds & Bad Debt / Cr 1100 or 1110 receivable
structured_data.on_later_recovery: post as a new event; never delete the write-off

title: The period close, in the order the steps depend on each other
content: Closing a period is a sequence, and doing it out of order produces a set of figures that were true at different moments. Capture every transaction of the period first, from both cash sources. Reconcile cash and the payment processor to external statements. Post accruals for costs incurred and not invoiced, and release the portion of every prepayment consumed. Recognise the revenue whose obligations were satisfied and release the corresponding deferred revenue. Post depreciation. Review the receivable and payable ageing and act on what it shows. Only then take the trial balance and produce the statements. Finally, lock the period so that later entries land in the next one and any correction to a locked period is an explicit, visible adjustment rather than a silent rewrite of a number already reported.

order: revenue recognition and deferred revenue release

title: Closing revenue and expense into retained earnings
content: Revenue and expense accounts are temporary: they measure one period and start the next at zero. At the year end their net balance is transferred to 3100 Retained Earnings, which is permanent and carries the accumulated result of every period the company has traded. Balance sheet accounts are never closed in this way; their balances roll forward because they describe a position at a moment rather than a flow across a span. The practical consequence for reporting is that a revenue figure is always 'for a period' and a cash figure is always 'as at a date', and a report that omits which one it is showing is ambiguous in a way that changes the reader's conclusion.

structured_data.reporting_rule: flows are 'for a period', positions are 'as at a date'

title: Correcting a posted entry: reverse and repost, never edit or delete
content: A posted entry is a historical record of what the books said. Correcting it by editing the amount or deleting the row destroys the evidence that the earlier figure was ever reported, and every downstream report produced from it becomes unexplainable. The correct method is to post a reversing entry, dated in the period where the correction is allowed to land, with a description naming the entry being corrected and why; then post the correct entry. Two visible entries and one explanation is the audit trail. If the original period is closed, the correction lands in the open period and the effect on the previously reported figure is disclosed rather than absorbed. The exception nobody should look for is that there is no exception: an entry that must not have existed is reversed, not erased.

method: post a reversal referencing the original
disclose the effect if the original period was reported

title: The income statement: what it measures and what it deliberately excludes
content: The income statement measures performance across a period: revenue earned, the costs incurred to earn it, and the result. It excludes anything that is a movement of position rather than a result of trading, which is why owner capital introduced, a loan drawn, and cash collected from a prior period's sale never appear on it. Structure matters as much as the total: revenue less cost of sales gives gross profit, which says whether the thing being sold is worth selling; gross profit less operating expenses gives the operating result, which says whether the company running it is affordable. Collapsing those into one net figure hides which of the two is the problem, and for a marketplace the two are almost always failing for different reasons.

title: The balance sheet: a position at a moment, in liquidity order
content: The balance sheet states what the company owns, what it owes and what is left for the owner, all as at one date. Assets are presented most liquid first, which is why cash leads and fixed assets trail; liabilities are presented by when they fall due. Reading it is mostly about relationships rather than totals: cash against near-term liabilities says whether the company can meet its obligations; receivables against a period's revenue says how long money takes to arrive; deferred revenue says how much of the cash held is not yet the company's to keep. A balance sheet that balances is not evidence of accuracy, because it balances by construction; the evidence is that each line reconciles to something outside the ledger.

structured_data.ordering: assets by liquidity, liabilities by maturity
reads: deferred revenue as an obligation not a cushion

title: The cash flow statement, and why profit and cash diverge
content: The cash flow statement explains the movement in cash across a period, split into operating, investing and financing activities. The indirect method starts from the profit figure and reverses everything in it that was not cash: add back depreciation, adjust for the movement in receivables, payables, prepayments and deferred revenue. The direct method lists actual receipts and payments instead. A profitable company runs out of cash when its receivables grow faster than its collections or when it prepays a year of costs in one month, and the cash flow statement is the only one of the three that shows this happening. Any report that presents profit as though it were available money is misleading even when every underlying figure is correct.

structured_data.indirect_method: start from profit, add back non-cash items, adjust for working capital movements
structured_data.why_it_matters: a profitable company can still be unable to pay

title: How the three statements tie together, and the checks that prove it
content: The three statements are one model seen from three angles and they are checkable against each other. The profit on the income statement, less any distribution, is the movement in retained earnings on the balance sheet. The closing cash on the cash flow statement equals the cash line on the balance sheet. The cash flow statement's starting profit is the income statement's result. When any of these three ties fails, the statements are not merely inconsistent, one of them is wrong, and the tie that broke names where to look. Producing a set of statements without running these three checks is publishing an untested claim.

ties: profit less distributions = movement in retained earnings
closing cash on the cash flow = cash on the balance sheet
cash flow opens with the income statement result
structured_data.rule: run all three ties before publishing

title: Working capital and the cash conversion cycle
content: Working capital is current assets less current liabilities: what the company has that will turn into cash soon, against what it must pay soon. The cash conversion cycle turns that stock figure into a duration by asking how many days money spends in receivables and inventory before it comes back, less how many days the company holds supplier money before paying. Shortening it releases cash without earning a single additional unit of revenue, which is why it is usually the cheapest liquidity available to a young company. For a marketplace with no inventory, the whole cycle is the gap between recognising a fee and collecting it, and that gap is a policy choice about payment terms rather than an accounting outcome.

structured_data.cycle: days in receivables + days in inventory - days in payables
structured_data.marketplace_case: with no inventory the cycle is the fee-to-collection gap

title: Gross margin, contribution and net result: three margins that answer three questions
content: Gross margin is revenue less the costs that vary directly with delivering it, and it answers whether the product is worth selling at all. Contribution margin subtracts all variable costs including variable selling costs, and it answers how much each additional unit pays towards the fixed base. The net result subtracts everything, and it answers whether the whole company is affordable at the current volume. Quoting one of these as 'the margin' without saying which it is makes comparison across periods meaningless, because the same business improves on one while worsening on another. For this marketplace, the costs that belong above the gross line are those that would not be incurred if the transaction had not happened, and payment processing fees are the clearest example.

structured_data.gross_margin: revenue less directly variable delivery costs
structured_data.rule: always name which margin is quoted

title: Burn and runway, and the arithmetic error that makes runway look longer than it is
content: Net burn is cash out less cash in over a period. Runway is cash held divided by net burn, expressed in months. Two errors make a reported runway wrong in the optimistic direction. The first is dividing by an average burn that includes a month with an unusual inflow, so the denominator is not a run rate at all; a total over thirty days is a total, and calling it a rate requires evidence that the period was representative. The second is counting cash the company holds but does not own, such as amounts sitting in deferred revenue or refunds payable, as though it were available. Runway computed on cash net of committed obligations is the only version worth reporting.

structured_data.net_burn: cash out less cash in for the period
structured_data.runway: available cash divided by monthly net burn
errors: treating a one-off period total as a run rate
counting deferred revenue and refunds payable as available cash

title: Materiality: deciding what is worth chasing, without using it as an excuse
content: Materiality is the threshold at which an error or omission would change a reader's decision. It is a judgement about the reader, not a percentage handed down, and it is set before the work rather than after a difference is found. Two rules stop it from becoming a licence. First, an immaterial difference that is not understood is still a control finding, because a small unexplained difference and a large one have the same cause until proved otherwise. Second, materiality never applies to items where the nature rather than the size carries the meaning: a related-party transaction, a fraud, or a breach of an obligation is material at any amount. Recording the threshold that was used, and when it was set, is part of the work.

structured_data.definition: the threshold at which an omission or error would change a reader's decision
structured_data.set: before the work, not after the difference is found

title: Going concern: the assumption underneath every other figure
content: Financial statements are normally prepared on the assumption that the company will continue trading for the foreseeable future. That assumption is what allows a fixed asset to be carried at cost less depreciation rather than at what it would fetch tomorrow. When the assumption is in doubt, the figures change and so does the disclosure, so the assessment is made deliberately rather than left implicit. The evidence is forward-looking and mostly about cash: committed inflows, committed outflows, available facilities, and the owner's stated intention and capacity to fund. The honest position when the evidence is thin is to state what is known and what is not, because a going-concern judgement asserted without evidence is exactly the kind of claim this seat is forbidden to make.

structured_data.assumption: the entity continues trading for the foreseeable future
structured_data.if_uncertain: state the uncertainty rather than assert the conclusion

title: What a published figure must carry beside it
content: A number on its own is not a report. Every figure this seat publishes carries the period or date it covers, the basis it was prepared on, the currency, and a route back to the rows it came from. Where a figure could not be measured it is reported as unknown with the reason, and never defaulted to zero, because zero is itself a measurement and a reader cannot tell a real zero from an absent one. Where a figure changed from a previously published version, the change is stated rather than left for the reader to notice. These are not presentational preferences: each one is the difference between a figure a reader can act on and a figure a reader has to trust.

structured_data.unknown_rule: report unknown with a reason; never default to zero
structured_data.restatement_rule: state any change from a previously published figure

title: Reconciling two cashflow sources when neither is the whole truth
content: Reconciliation is not comparing two totals. It is explaining every difference between two independent records of the same events until nothing unexplained remains. Take each source separately, list the items in one that are absent from the other, and classify each difference as timing, missing entry, error, or genuine scope difference. A timing difference resolves itself in the next period and is recorded as such. A missing entry is posted. An error is corrected by reversal. A scope difference means the two sources were never measuring the same thing and the reconciliation was mis-specified. What is never permitted is a balancing figure: an adjustment posted to make two totals agree without knowing what it represents converts an unexplained difference into an explained-looking one, which is worse than leaving it visible.

method: list items in A absent from B and vice versa
classify each as timing, missing, error, or scope
structured_data.forbidden: a balancing or plug figure posted to force agreement

title: Bank reconciliation: the ledger against the statement
content: The bank reconciliation starts from the ledger balance for 1000 Cash & Bank and the closing balance on the bank statement, and explains the gap. The usual explanations are payments issued and not yet cleared, receipts recorded and not yet credited, and bank-originated items the company has not yet recorded such as charges and interest. The first two are timing and need no entry; the third needs an entry, because the bank knows something the ledger does not. The reconciliation is complete when the two balances agree after listed reconciling items, and every item on that list has a date and an expected clearance. Items that sit on the list across several periods are not reconciling items any more, they are unresolved differences, and they get investigated rather than carried forward again.

structured_data.aged_item_rule: an item carried across several periods is an unresolved difference, not a reconciling item

title: The payment processor clearing account, and why gross matters
content: A payment processor collects from the customer, deducts its fee, and remits the remainder some days later. Recording only the remittance loses two facts at once: the revenue was larger than the cash, and a fee was incurred. The clearing account exists to keep both. On the transaction, debit 1050 Stripe Clearing for the gross amount and credit revenue. On the fee, debit 6100 Payment Processing Fees and credit 1050. On the payout, debit 1000 Cash & Bank and credit 1050. The balance left in 1050 at any date should equal the transactions collected but not yet paid out, which is a directly testable figure against the processor's own balance. Netting the fee against revenue instead understates both revenue and cost and makes gross margin uncomputable.

structured_data.on_fee: Dr 6100 Payment Processing Fees / Cr 1050 Stripe Clearing
structured_data.on_payout: Dr 1000 Cash & Bank / Cr 1050 Stripe Clearing
structured_data.error: netting the fee against revenue destroys gross margin

title: Segregation of duties in a company with almost no people
content: The control principle is that the person who initiates a transaction should not be the person who approves it and should not be the person who records it, because one person holding all three can create and conceal a fictitious transaction. A very small company cannot fully achieve this, and pretending otherwise is worse than admitting it. What compensates: every transaction traces to an external document the company did not create, approval for defined classes is held by a different party from the one recording, records are append-only so concealment requires a visible reversal, and someone reviews the resulting reports against expectation. In this company the founder's ruling already separates two classes of decision from the seat that records them, refunds and advertising spend, and that separation is the control rather than a formality.

structured_data.principle: initiation, approval and recording should not sit with one party
compensating_controls: approval held elsewhere for defined classes
structured_data.honest_limit: full segregation is unachievable at this headcount and is not claimed

title: The audit trail: what makes a set of books defensible later
content: An audit trail lets a reader who was not present reconstruct, for any figure, what happened, when it was recorded, on what evidence, and by whom. It requires three things that must be designed in rather than added afterwards: source documents retained and addressable, entries that reference those documents, and records that are append-only so that history cannot be rewritten. The test of an audit trail is not whether it exists but whether it survives a hostile question: pick a published figure at random, and see whether it can be walked back to source documents without asking anyone to remember anything. A trail that depends on recollection is not a trail.

structured_data.test: pick a published figure and walk it to source without relying on memory

title: Suspense and unmatched items: hold, do not force
content: When a transaction cannot be classified, the two available actions are to hold it unposted and chase the missing information, or to post it to a clearly named holding account with an owner and a due date. What is not available is to post it to a plausible account so that the books look complete. A holding account is acceptable only while it is small, aged, reviewed and shrinking; a holding balance that grows across periods means classification has stopped happening and the reports built on those books are describing a company that does not exist. Every item in a holding account carries what is missing and who is chasing it, so that the balance is a work list rather than a place things go to be forgotten.

allowed: post to a named holding account with owner and due date
structured_data.forbidden: posting to a plausible account to make the books look complete

title: Detecting a duplicate receipt before it becomes a duplicate expense
content: A receipt arriving twice, forwarded twice, or issued as both a proforma and a final invoice, becomes a doubled cost if each is posted on its own merits. The check is a match on the combination that identifies the underlying transaction rather than the document: supplier, amount, currency and transaction date, with the document number as a secondary signal because different systems number the same charge differently. A candidate duplicate is held for review rather than discarded, because a genuine pair of identical monthly charges exists and discarding it silently understates cost. Recording the decision, duplicate or genuine, means the same pair is not re-examined every month.

structured_data.record: the duplicate-or-genuine decision, so it is not re-litigated

title: Cut-off: which period a transaction belongs to
content: Cut-off is the decision about which period an event falls in, and it is decided by when the economic event happened rather than when the paperwork arrived or the payment cleared. A service consumed in one month and invoiced in the next belongs to the month it was consumed. A payment made in advance belongs to the periods it covers. The reason cut-off gets its own name and its own test is that cut-off errors do not fail loudly: both periods still balance, the trial balance is unaffected, and the only symptom is that one period looks better than it was and the next looks worse. Testing it means taking transactions either side of the period boundary and checking the date of the underlying event against the period they landed in.

structured_data.decided_by: the date of the economic event
structured_data.why_it_hides: both periods still balance; only the split is wrong
structured_data.test: sample transactions either side of the boundary against event dates

title: Currency precision, rounding, and where a difference of one fils comes from
content: AED is subdivided into 100 fils, so the ledger's smallest unit is 0.01. Amounts are stored and compared at that precision, and a percentage-derived figure such as a commission is rounded once at the point it becomes an amount rather than carried at full precision into a later comparison. Rounding at more than one point in a calculation chain produces differences that are individually trivial and collectively unexplainable. Where a difference of a single unit appears in a reconciliation, the cause is almost always either double rounding or a foreign-currency conversion applied at a different rate or a different moment by the two sources, and finding which is faster than absorbing it. Storing money as a binary floating-point number is its own separate cause of these differences and is not how monetary amounts are held.

structured_data.rule: round once, at the point a rate becomes an amount
usual_causes_of_a_one_unit_difference: different FX rate or timestamp between sources

title: Reading a variance: one number can have three causes
content: A cost line that moved is not yet a finding. The move has a price component, a volume component, and a mix or classification component, and they call for different actions. A software cost that doubled because usage doubled is a scale story; the same figure because a vendor raised its rate is a negotiation; the same figure again because a cost was reclassified out of another line is not a movement at all. Decomposing before reporting is what stops a report generating the wrong action. The same discipline applies to a favourable variance: a cost that fell because an invoice has not arrived yet is an accrual that was missed, and reporting it as a saving is reporting a bookkeeping gap as a business result.

structured_data.favourable_variance_trap: a cost that fell because an invoice is missing is a missed accrual, not a saving
